builder_plan.scenario: Profiling shows attention computation is a bottleneck in your self-hosted service.
builder_plan.change: Check the supported GPU, tensor shapes, and precision, then replace only the relevant kernel.
builder_plan.baseline: The existing kernel inside the same complete serving pipeline.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Numerical differences, end-to-end latency, throughput, and memory at realistic shapes.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Easy Multi-Precision Acceleration via Vectorization
summary: The method replaces hand-written, hardware-specific low-level kernels (CUDA/assembly or per-generation tuning) with high-level vectorized matrix operations that map onto accelerator BLAS/FFT libraries across precisions and hardware generations. The cost is dependence on the quality of the underlying vendor libraries, limited control for irregular or fused operations, and potential sub-peak results for workloads outside dense linear algebra and FFT convolution. It can fail when a workload is dominated by custom fused kernels, small or irregular shapes, or when lower-precision paths introduce accuracy loss the application cannot tolerate.
rationale: The paper demonstrates that standard high-level vectorized code already reaches near-peak throughput on a single modern GPU for exactly the dense operations that dominate ML inference, so the reader should prefer these abstractions over custom kernel work.

claims.statement: The method replaces hand-written, hardware-specific low-level kernels (CUDA/assembly or per-generation tuning) with high-level vectorized matrix operations that map onto accelerator BLAS/FFT libraries across precisions and hardware generations. The cost is dependence on the quality of the underlying vendor libraries, limited control for irregular or fused operations, and potential sub-peak results for workloads outside dense linear algebra and FFT convolution. It can fail when a workload is dominated by custom fused kernels, small or irregular shapes, or when lower-precision paths introduce accuracy loss the application cannot tolerate.

Near hardware peak performance is readily accessible from high-level vectorized code for memory bandwidth, FP64/FP32/FP16 real and complex GEMM, and FFT-based 2D convolution across hardware spanning nearly a decade.
